title: Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models
summary: This continuation plans integral local models from polynomial Schubert closures and minuscule Hodge embeddings to normal scheme representatives, tangent spaces spanned by formal curves, same-residue-field Schubert curves, EL/PEL Drinfeld comparisons and connected geometric tubes. It keeps general-bound v-sheaves separate from minuscule scheme models and records the precise modular-representation, algebraic-loop and cohomological supplier gaps. The independent rational Gelfand commutativity proof receives an exhaustive split brief.
readme: The definitive reader is research/blueprint/readmes/GeometricSatakeAndFusionPartII.md. Its nine layers distinguish polynomial closures, canonical normal schemes, general-bound v-sheaves, scheme tangent spaces and tube cohomology. The 158-item assignment ledger includes 129 local-model items and 29 items in the independent rational Gelfand-proof split. Every layer is planned; supplier and source gaps are explicit, so the packet is complete but not closed.

stages.title: Data and conventions
stages.description: Define the minuscule datum, Hodge and abelian types, quasi-tame/essentially tame ranges, v-closure and scheme specifications, and goodness. Pin reflex bases, full versus connected fixers and the subspace/quotient/opposite-cocharacter dictionary.

stages.title: Polynomial closures and comparisons
stages.description: Build polynomial BD modification spaces and their schematic closures. Establish normality and component geometry in the prime-to-p range; prove polynomial adjoint comparisons, the auxiliary Hodge cover and the one-lattice GL comparison.

stages.title: Polynomial and lattice embeddings
stages.description: Prove the Weil-split, Weyl-lattice and restriction-of-structure embeddings in their precise facet ranges, their power and symplectic-chain consequences, the GL incidence model, period-total embedding and trace symplectic construction.

stages.title: Canonical schemes and kimberlites
stages.description: Identify the classical auxiliary construction with the v-closure using the existing normal-recovery theorem. Plan normalization of images and endomorphism cutouts. Compare companion, Witt and v-special fibres; prove general-bound kimberlite properties and general minuscule weak normal representability.

stages.title: Tangent geometry
stages.description: Define the span of formal-curve derivatives using the existing tangent carrier. Develop root and Cartan bounds using minuscule test modules, retaining the quaternionic-D restriction. Identify reductive Weil-restriction fibres with summed Schubert bounds and prove their curve-spanning endpoints.

stages.title: Curves over the same residue field
stages.description: Import the finite invariant-coroot step; supply the valued-root and rank-one flag adapters, split and unitary curves, rational positive-loop lifting and the same-residue-field curve theorem at very special level.

stages.title: EL and PEL examples
stages.description: Define module chains with periodicity and polarization line, their torsors and the naive determinant quotient functor. Construct the B_dR⁺ kernel comparison. Prove the EL and unitary Drinfeld local-model comparisons with correct signature weights and lattice levels.

stages.title: Tubes and unrestricted normality
stages.description: Compute tube components by lowest nearby-cycle stalks. Combine the admissible S₂ and two-translation inputs with an early Wakimoto filtration to prove connected tubes for all bounds. Deduce unrestricted minuscule normal representability, good acceptable embeddings and the admissible lattice criterion.

stages.title: Nearby cycles and test functions
stages.description: Prove splitting-field monodromy and its very-special strengthening in the tame polynomial range. Define the unshifted semisimple trace with geometric Frobenius; prove parahoric centrality and the unramified minuscule Bernstein characterization with all shifts, half twists and measures fixed.
